name: Wendigo Mane
summary: Across Dun Morogh, wendigos roam the frozen crags, and their manes keep the mountain cold at bay. Pilot Stonegear has a use for them.

sections.title: Warmth for the Ironworks
sections.body: Wendigos roam the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, their coarse fur guarding them from bitter drafts. Outside Kharanos, Pilot Stonegear sends adventurers to Grizzled Den for their heavy manes. He means to weave them into an insulating rug for the interior deck of Trollplow, his prized dwarven siege engine.

faq.q: What creatures yield a Wendigo Mane?
faq.answer: Wendigo manes come from wendigos in Dun Morogh’s snows. They include Young Wendigos, adult Wendigos, and alpha beasts such as Vagash, Edan the Howler, and Old Icebeard.

faq.q: Why does Pilot Stonegear want these manes?
faq.answer: Pilot Stonegear wants the manes for an insulating rug on the interior deck of Trollplow, his siege engine. The thick fur will help keep his station warm as the machine travels through frozen terrain.

faq.q: Where is the best place to find wendigos for their manes?
faq.answer: Pilot Stonegear recommends Grizzled Den, a cave system in the mountains directly west of Kharanos. Wendigos fill the cavern and its surrounding slopes.
Yes. Wendigos are feral, territorial predators with great strength and thick hides. Dwarven trainers regard facing them in their dens as an early test of a mountaineer’s courage and fighting grit.

angles.text: Dwarven machinery in Dun Morogh has freezing metal cockpits. Wendigo pelts make practical insulating linings.
Young dwarves hunt the wendigos of Grizzled Den to prove their toughness to Kharanos veterans.
